title: Prefetch Coalescer — experiment log & handover
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the week-long run of the prefetch coalescer experiment (prototype: prefetch-coalescer-v2) and the handover notes for next sprint. Goal was to reduce tail latency for short chat sessions (<=128 tokens) by coalescing KV cache prefetch across concurrent microbatches while preserving p50 throughput. We landed a small kernel scheduler patch and a KV eviction heuristic tweak to support variable prefetch budgets.

What we changed (high-level):
- Kernel scheduler: added `micro_slot_coalesce` flag (toggle) to allow up to 3 microbatch prefetches to share an inflight kernel invocation. Implemented in ks-scheduler.c (PR #4123).
- KV cache: introduced a soft prefetch budget per-connection (config: kv.prefetch_budget = 4096 tokens) and LRU-aged prefetch pruning to avoid memory spikes.
- Batching layer: small change to batch assembly to mark prefetchable prefixes and annotate request metadata so runtime knows safe coalescing boundaries.
- Canary routing: new rollout policy routed 5% of chat traffic for model-7b variants through the experiment pool (dedicated GPU cluster test nodes).

Experiments run (dates: 2026-03-04 through 2026-03-10):
- Run A — baseline: production snapshot without coalescer (control). 72h window.
- Run B — coalescer enabled, prefetch_budget=4096, micro_slot_coalesce=2. 48h window.
- Run C — coalescer enabled, prefetch_budget=2048, micro_slot_coalesce=3 with LRU-prune aggressive. 24h window.

Key metrics (aggregated):
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 per-token latency (short sessions): 12ms / 52ms / 210ms
- Run B p50/p95/p99: 11.2ms / 38ms / 160ms (p95 improvement ~27%)
- Run C p50/p95/p99: 11.6ms / 34ms / 145ms (tail improved most, but CPU context increased)
- Throughput (tokens/sec per-GPU) slightly down in Run C (-4%) due to extra coalescing overhead; Run B stable (within +/-1%).
- Memory: Run C showed peak KV memory +9% on the canary nodes; aggressive prune mitigated sustained growth.

Observations & notes:
- Coalescing helps p95/p99 primarily on short sequences where prefetch dominates. For long sequences (>512 tokens) effect is neutral or slightly negative.
- The kernel patch reduces kernel-launch overhead but increases CPU scheduling pressure in the host when micro_slot_coalesce>=3. We saw a small uptick in context-switches and syscalls (profiling attached in PR).
- LRU-aged prefetch prune must be tuned per-cluster; the default aggressive setting caused jitter on low-memory hosts.
- Some edge cases found: (1) clients that OOM mid-request and retry caused duplicate prefetch metadata—added idempotency guard in batching commit. (2) A small race where a microbatch split across threads could double-count prefetch budget; fixed with an atomic increment.

Known issues / risks:
- Memory regression on older GPU nodes (A100 gen1) if prefetch budget set too high. Mitigation: automatic downgrade of prefetch_budget based on host.available_kv_mb at registration time.
- Observability gaps: we need a histogram of coalesced microbatch sizes in the Console (per-route) to correlate with cost. Filed SRV-9889.
- Canary coverage: only 5% traffic — we might miss rare combinatorial failures. Consider a short spike to 20% during off-peak to validate.

Decisions made this week:
- Keep micro_slot_coalesce default = 2 for next sprint; expose as runtime knob per-pool.
- Use prefetch_budget=4096 as default for dedicated pools; make it adaptive for private deployments.
- Do not enable coalescer for models flagged as "long-context-optimized" by model-catalog.

Next actions (owners):
- Finalize PR #4123 tests and perf regression checks — Liam Chen — due 2026-03-15.
- Add per-route coalesced-microbatch histogram to Console metrics — Sofia Martinez + Observability — due 2026-03-22 (linked SRV-9889).
- Implement host-level prefetch_budget auto-downgrade on registration (small patch to node-agent) — Jonah Rivers — due 2026-03-19.
- Prepare canary 20% off-peak run and rollback playbook, coordinate with SRE — Mei Huang & SRE — window 2026-03-21 02:00-06:00 UTC.
- Create a short runbook for Solutions Eng describing behavior and opt-out knob for Dedicated customers — Asha Patel — due 2026-03-18.

Handover notes for next sprint:
- Focus on observability first: without histograms and p99-by-coalesced-size we won't be able to tune defaults safely.
- Keep kernel changes minimal; prefer micro-optimizations that don't increase host CPU overhead.
- Experiment owners should attach flamegraphs and host-level syscall traces to PRs for any scheduler tweak.

Appendix / quick links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123 (kernel scheduler)
- Jira: SRV-9876 (prefetch coalescer epic), SRV-9889 (observability), SRV-9892 (canary rollout plan)
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/runtime-experiments/C04A9/thread-78
- Test harness: internal bench harness command: tools/bench/run_prefetch_coalesce --model model-7b --workload short-chat --canary 5

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Try a graded backoff for micro_slot_coalesce (2 -> 3 only if host.cpu_nice < 0.2).
- Revisit prefetch_budget units; consider switching to percent-of-kv_mem to simplify cross-node defaults.
- Add a note in the kernels README about prefetch idempotency edge.

Status: In review with Eng and Observability; will merge when PR has full perf CI and we've scheduled the 20% canary run.
